_about: The 160 competencies (section 5.3): 135 technical (scale 0-4), 23 Lexonis cross-functional and 2 Lexonis functional (scale 1-4, two cross-functional ones use 0-4). externalId = Lexonis key.

competencies.name: Asset Inventory and CMDB Integration
competencies.description: The ability to maintain complete, accurate, and continuously updated records of enterprise servers and related configuration data within asset inventory and CMDB systems. It ensures effective visibility, traceability, and alignment between patch management, vulnerability remediation, and compliance reporting processes.

competencies.name: Access Management
competencies.description: The ability to define, enforce, review, and optimize access control models, including entitlements, RBAC and policy engines, to uphold least privilege, enforce segregation of duties, and enable real-time risk mitigation across data, applications, and infrastructure.

competencies.name: Attack-Path & Kill-Chain Engineering
competencies.description: The ability to transform threat-intelligence and reconnaissance data into multi-stage kill-chains that reveal exploitable infrastructure, user-journey and process weak points, enabling the design and execution of realistic, high-impact attack paths across both IT and OT environments in a global Oil and Gas context.

competencies.name: Application Security
competencies.description: The ability to effectively identify, assess, mitigate, and manage application security risks throughout the software development lifecycle.

competencies.name: Application Security Development
competencies.description: The ability to embed security throughout the software development and lifecycle management process by ensuring that applications are designed, built, deployed, and maintained to proactively prevent, detect, and remediate vulnerabilities. This includes the integration of secure architecture principles, AI-assisted development tools, threat modelling, secure coding, automation of security controls, validation pipelines, and governance of third-party and custom-built application components.

competencies.name: Application Security Review
competencies.description: The ability to perform in-depth application security reviews across the software development lifecycle by leveraging structured review processes, code analysis techniques, and AI-assisted tools. This includes evaluating design choices, inspecting code and architecture for vulnerabilities, and applying machine learning models to accelerate and enhance threat identification and secure remediation.

competencies.name: APT Tracking & Attribution CTI
competencies.description: The ability to correlate technical indicators, malware artefacts, network telemetry, TTPs, with geopolitical context, sector-specific targeting patterns, and business-line intelligence to attribute intrusions to Advanced Persistent Threat (APT) actors, determine their motivations, and shape defence and mitigation strategies for the enterprise.

competencies.name: Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery Strategy and Planning
competencies.description: The ability to design, implement, and govern the organisation's Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery strategies in alignment with ISO 22301 standard, integrating cybersecurity resilience, threat intelligence, and regulatory compliance to ensure organizational preparedness, operational recovery, and sustained critical function continuity.

competencies.name: BCDR Testing, Exercise and Awareness Management
competencies.description: The ability to plan, execute, and govern business continuity and disaster recovery (BCDR) testing, simulation exercises, and awareness programs that validate organizational readiness, enhance recovery capabilities, and build resilience culture in alignment with standards such as ISO 22301, and sector-specific requirements.

competencies.name: Business Impact Analysis (BIA)
competencies.description: The ability to plan, conduct, and govern Business Impact Analyses (BIA) to identify critical business and technical functions, assess disruption impacts, and to inform continuity strategies, recovery priorities, and risk mitigation in alignment with ISO 22301 standard and sector-specific requirements.

competencies.name: Backup and Recovery Technologies
competencies.description: The ability to design, implement, manage, and govern backup and recovery technologies and procedures to ensure data integrity, availability, and rapid restoration of services across enterprise IT, OT, and cloud environments, in alignment with business continuity and regulatory requirements.

competencies.name: Business Service Dependency Mapping
competencies.description: The ability to identify and document end-to-end service architecture, business-critical dependencies, and technical interconnections across IT and OT domains, enabling effective continuity planning and impact containment.

competencies.name: Cybersecurity and Business Partnering
competencies.description: The ability to advise and guide business and cybersecurity stakeholders on aligning risk and compliance priorities to ensure that security objectives are balanced with operational needs, safety considerations, and business value across IT, OT, and shared-service environments.

competencies.name: Cyber Assurance Governance
competencies.description: The ability to advise and guide on the planning, execution, and governance of cyber assurance assessments across IT and OT to ensure control effectiveness is independently validated, evidence is audit-ready, and remediation responsibilities are clearly assigned within a shared-service model.

competencies.name: Cloud Automation and Scripting
competencies.description: The ability to design and implement scripts, API integrations, and infrastructure-as-code (IaC) to automate the enforcement of security controls, collection of cloud telemetry, and remediation of vulnerabilities or misconfigurations at scale.

competencies.name: Cybersecurity Data Lake
competencies.description: The ability to design, operate, and leverage cybersecurity data lakes to ingest, normalize, correlate, and analyze diverse security telemetry (e.g., vulnerability data, patch status, threat indicators, cloud configurations) to support detection, risk prioritization, remediation tracking, and strategic decision-making using automation and AI.

competencies.name: Cyber Exercise & Operational Intelligence Support
competencies.description: The ability to embed targeted, high-fidelity threat intelligence into cybersecurity drills, Security Operations Center (SOC) workflows, and time-sensitive operations, delivering actionable insights that sharpen defensive playbooks, accelerate analyst decision-making, and measurably improve the organization's readiness against adversaries targeting critical assets.

competencies.name: Cloud Identity Management
competencies.description: The ability to manage and govern identities, roles, secrets, and access policies across multi-cloud environments, integrating with on-premises directories to enforce Zero Trust principles, least-privilege access, and continuous compliance.

competencies.name: Cybersecurity Incident Management, Response, and Coordination
competencies.description: The ability to detect, assess, respond to, and coordinate resolution of cybersecurity incidents across IT and OT environments, ensuring minimal business disruption, effective containment, and rapid recovery in alignment with global best practices (e.g., NIST SP 800-61, ISO/IEC 27035, IEC 62443 for OT).

competencies.name: Crisis Management
competencies.description: The ability to prepare for, respond to, and lead organizational crisis situations by activating structured plans, enabling informed decision-making, managing internal and external communication, and ensuring coordinated recovery efforts in alignment with standards such as ISO 22361, ISO 22301, and NIST crisis coordination practices.

competencies.name: Cyber Risk Governance & Strategy
competencies.description: The ability to define and implement cybersecurity risk governance models, strategies, and frameworks aligned with the organisation's business objectives, risk appetite, and UAE regulatory requirements.

competencies.name: Cloud Security Architecture
competencies.description: The ability to designs secure cloud architectures by integrating workload protection, identity and access control, and network segmentation using cloud-native capabilities and layered security models.

competencies.name: Collection Strategy & Data-Source Prioritization
competencies.description: The ability to transforms PIRs into focused collection plans selecting and prioritizing the most valuable data sources aligned to mission-critical assets and the evolving threat landscape.

competencies.name: Cloud Security Monitoring
competencies.description: The ability to monitor security events across cloud platforms (e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP) by analyzing logs, detecting misconfigurations, access misuse, and cloud-native threats.

competencies.name: Cloud Security Management
competencies.description: The ability to operationalize and govern cloud security architectures, services, and controls across IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS environments, leveraging provider-native tools, container and workload protection platforms, and AI-driven analytics to secure data, applications, identities, and infrastructure. This includes implementing defense-in-depth strategies, managing compliance, and enabling secure-by-design engineering practices across public, private, hybrid, and multi-cloud deployments.

competencies.name: Cyber Security Management System (CSMS)
competencies.description: The ability to implement, operate, and continuously enhance a Cyber Security Management System (CSMS) that satisfies ISA/IEC 62443, ISO 27001, and UAE regulatory mandates while safeguarding production, safety, and corporate objectives.

competencies.name: Cloud Services Patch Management
competencies.description: The ability to plan, automate, and govern Windows and Linux patching across cloud environments (AWS, Azure, GCP) to ensure systems remain secure, reliable, and compliant.

competencies.name: Cloud Security Risk Management
competencies.description: The ability to identify, evaluate, and govern cloud-security risks, ensuring compliant, resilient, and cost-optimised cloud operations across the enterprise.

competencies.name: Continuity Testing & BC/DR Exercise Management
competencies.description: The ability to design, execute, and manage structured continuity testing programs, including business continuity and disaster recovery (BC/DR) drills, tabletop exercises, and technical validation of backup and recovery systems.

competencies.name: Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI)
competencies.description: The ability to collect, enrich, analyze, and operationalize threat data and adversary behaviors to produce actionable intelligence that informs cybersecurity defense, detection, response, risk mitigation, and strategic decision-making across IT and OT environments.

competencies.name: Cyber Threat Intelligence for OT
competencies.description: The ability to collect, analyse, and apply cyber-threat intelligence that is specific to Operational Technology (OT) and industrial control systems (ICS) used in Oil & Gas operations, transforming raw data on adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) into actionable insights that protect safety-critical processes, guide security controls, and inform continuity and resilience decisions.

competencies.name: Cybersecurity Vendor Management
competencies.description: The ability to assess, select, onboard, monitor, and govern external cybersecurity vendors and service providers to ensure they meet organizational security, operational, regulatory, and resilience requirements across all domains including threat intelligence, continuity, SOC, testing, and cloud services.

competencies.name: Data Analytics for Cybersecurity
competencies.description: The ability to collect, normalize, analyze, and visualize security-relevant data to detect anomalies, interpret adversary behavior, assess control effectiveness, and support risk-informed decision-making across both IT and OT environments.

competencies.name: Data-Diode & Unidirectional-Gateway Engineering
competencies.description: The ability to design, deploy, and maintain data-diode solutions to securely transfer OT data one-way, preventing inbound threats and ensuring compliance with UAE cybersecurity and energy sector standards.

competencies.name: Detection Engineering
competencies.description: The ability to design, tune, and validate detection logic, including analytics, correlation rules, and signatures, that reliably identifies malicious activity across diverse environments while minimizing false positives and operational noise.

competencies.name: Digital Forensics
competencies.description: The ability to collect, preserve, analyze, and present digital evidence to support investigations of computer-related incidents maintain its integrity for use in legal proceedings, incident response, or other investigative purposes.

competencies.name: Data Incident Response
competencies.description: The ability to triage, investigate, and assess data breaches by coordinating forensic analysis and response teams to contain impact, while ensuring timely reporting under UAE's PDPL 72-hour rule through regulator notifications, stakeholder communication, and proper documentation.

competencies.name: Data Loss Prevention (DLP)
competencies.description: The ability to deploy, calibrate, and monitor endpoint, email, and cloud-based DLP controls that detect, alert, and prevent unauthorized transmission or exfiltration of sensitive data.

competencies.name: Data Management Lifecycle
competencies.description: The ability to design and enforce data-classification schemas, handling rules, and retention schedules, applying labelling tools and automated workflows across converged OT and IT estates.

competencies.name: Deep Open-Source Intelligence (OSINT) Collection
competencies.description: The ability to systematically gathers and enriches open-source and dark-web data to inform red-team planning, craft convincing social-engineering lures, and pinpoint high-value initial-access vectors in the Oil & Gas sector.

competencies.name: Data Protection Governance
competencies.description: The ability to develop and deploy an enterprise data-protection governance model and strategic roadmap spanning privacy, classification, information lifecycle management, and data breach response integrating data protection laws standards with corporate risk appetite.

competencies.name: Data Privacy Impact Assessment (DPIA)
competencies.description: The ability to assess projects, systems, and third-party vendors for privacy risk by documenting lawful basis, data flows, risk mitigations, and residual impacts in accordance with the organisation's internal standards and UAE-specific regulatory mandates.

competencies.name: Digital Resilience & Cybersecurity Integration
competencies.description: The ability to embed cybersecurity requirements, threat intelligence insights, and cyber resilience principles into business continuity strategies, ensuring that both IT and OT environments are protected, recoverable, and adaptive to evolving threats.

competencies.name: Data Rights Management
competencies.description: The ability to orchestrate end-to-end workflows for data subject rights requests, including identity verification, data retrieval, redaction, and secure fulfillment, for access, rectification, erasure, and consent management.

competencies.name: Data Retention & Secure Disposal
competencies.description: The ability to align and enforce data retention and disposal practices by harmonizing legal hold obligations, operational needs, and UAE regulatory requirements.

competencies.name: Data Regulatory & Standards Interpretation
competencies.description: The ability to monitor, interpret and translate evolving UAE and international privacy regulations into actionable controls, updated policies, and enterprise-wide compliance roadmaps.

competencies.name: Enterprise Control and Assurance Framework
competencies.description: The ability to design and maintain cybersecurity control frameworks across IT and OT, standardizing testing, mapping risks, scoring criticality, and enabling traceable, evidence-based assurance aligned with policy, regulatory, and automation requirements.

competencies.name: Enterprise Cybersecurity Assurance Program Management
competencies.description: The ability to lead a cybersecurity assurance program, aligning assessments and projects to strategic objectives, standardizing methods, coordinating vendors, and delivering executive-level insight through metrics and governance.

competencies.name: Enterprise Risk Management Integration & Reporting
competencies.description: The ability to integrate cybersecurity risk management into Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) frameworks and report risk status and trends to senior governance bodies, executive stakeholders, and corporate risk committees.

competencies.name: Enterprise Security Architecture
competencies.description: The ability to design, assess, and govern secure digital infrastructure architectures across IT, OT, and cloud environments by embedding security-by-design principles, zero trust models, and AI-enabled threat prevention. This includes the development and maintenance of security reference architectures, the integration of governance and compliance requirements, and alignment with enterprise architecture to ensure consistent, resilient, and future-ready cybersecurity capabilities.

competencies.name: Endpoint Security (IT)
competencies.description: The ability to design, implement, operate, and govern security protections for individual computing devices (e.g., laptops, servers, mobile devices, virtual machines) across IT environment. This includes preventing, detecting, and responding to threats; managing endpoint security platforms; and enforcing policy compliance to protect the broader digital infrastructure.

competencies.name: Endpoint Security (OT)
competencies.description: The ability to secure industrial endpoint devices, such as PLCs, RTUs, HMIs, and safety systems, by applying security configuration, monitoring, and risk mitigation strategies that balance cybersecurity, operational continuity, and safety in OT environments. This includes assessing vulnerabilities, integrating OT and enterprise security capabilities, and ensuring compliance with industry-specific standards.

competencies.name: Emerging Threat Technologies and Tools Evaluation
competencies.description: The ability to identify, assess, and trial advanced threat intelligence platforms, data sources, and analytical tools to improve threat detection, attribution, and strategic foresight.

competencies.name: EDR/XDR Tooling
competencies.description: The ability to deploy, configure, and operationalize Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) and Extended Detection and Response (XDR) platforms to achieve comprehensive threat visibility, accelerate incident triage, and enable automated or analyst-driven response actions across endpoints, networks, and cloud environments.

competencies.name: IAM Architecture
competencies.description: The ability to design and evolve holistic IAM blueprints, reference patterns, and technology roadmaps that align identity capabilities with enterprise architecture, business strategy, performance objectives, and regulatory requirements.

competencies.name: IAM Automation
competencies.description: The ability to streamline identity lifecycle management, access provisioning, policy enforcement, and compliance reporting through automated workflows and integrations. It includes the ability to develop and maintain scripts, APIs, and orchestration tools that reduce manual effort, improve accuracy, and ensure timely access decisions.

competencies.name: IAM Application Integration
competencies.description: The ability to build, secure, and maintain REST/SCIM integrations, using tokens, webhooks, and service identities that synchronise identity data and extend IAM controls seamlessly into heterogeneous applications and platforms.

competencies.name: Internal Controls Evaluation for Resilience
competencies.description: The ability to systematically review, test, and enhance internal business, IT, OT, and third-party controls, spanning policies, processes, and technical safeguards to confirm they adequately protect critical operations and align with organizational resilience objectives.

competencies.name: IAM Governance
competencies.description: The ability to establish, measure, and enforce IAM policies, roles, workflows, and accountability structures to ensure identity decisions align with organizational goals, risk appetite, and stakeholder expectations.

competencies.name: IT Infrastructure and Cloud Resilience
competencies.description: The ability to design, implement, and govern resilient IT and cloud infrastructure architectures, ensuring system availability, recoverability, and continuity through redundancy, failover, and disaster recovery strategies aligned with industry standards (e.g., ISO 22301, CSA).

competencies.name: ICS/OT Penetration & Safety-Aware Testing
competencies.description: The ability to plan and executive penetration tests against industrial control systems and operational technology (OT) while preserving human / process safety, asset integrity and service in high hazard environments.

competencies.name: IAM for OT Systems
competencies.description: The ability to manage and secure human and machine identities in OT environments by enforcing least privilege, MFA, and access governance, aligned with IEC 62443, UAE mandates, and corporate cybersecurity standards.

competencies.name: Internal Security Audit
competencies.description: The ability to systematically evaluates an organization's information security controls, policies, and procedures through structured assessment methodologies to identify vulnerabilities, verify compliance with relevant standards, and provide actionable recommendations to enhance the overall security posture.

competencies.name: Information Security Awareness
competencies.description: The able to design and deliver awareness programs that embed UAE regulations and corporate data protection and privacy policies into daily practices promoting a culture of information security accountability across all business areas.

competencies.name: Information Security Governance and Regulatory Compliance
competencies.description: The ability to interpret, implement, monitor, and continuously improve information security governance frameworks and cybersecurity requirements from international standards, regional regulations, sector-specific directives, and contractual obligations, ensuring integrated cybersecurity controls across both IT and OT environments remain compliant.

competencies.name: Kubernetes Patch Management
competencies.description: The ability to plan, execute, and govern patching activities across Kubernetes clusters and their underlying components to ensure security, stability, and compliance.

competencies.name: Log Management
competencies.description: The ability to collect, normalize, store, and govern security-relevant log data to ensure its integrity, availability, and usability for threat monitoring, forensic investigation, and regulatory compliance.

competencies.name: Malware Analysis
competencies.description: The ability to dissect and analyze malicious code to uncover its functionality, identify behavioral patterns, extract indicators of compromise (IOCs), and recommend defensive measures to contain, mitigate, and prevent similar threats.

competencies.name: Network & Infrastructure Security
competencies.description: The ability to design, implement, monitor, and evolve secure, resilient, and compliant network infrastructure across IT and OT environments. This includes safeguarding traffic flows, enforcing segmentation, managing perimeter defenses, enabling secure remote access, and integrating DNS, web, and email security layers. The role also includes applying AI-enhanced analytics to optimize visibility, detect anomalies, and automate response across the enterprise network stack.

competencies.name: Network Security Monitoring
competencies.description: The ability to monitor and analyze network traffic using IDS, flow data, and packet analysis tools to detect and investigate suspicious activity, validate IOCs, and support incident response, ensuring early identification of threats across IT and OT environments.

competencies.name: OT Cybersecurity
competencies.description: The ability to assess, implement, and govern cybersecurity controls for Operational Technology (OT) and Industrial Control Systems (ICS), in accordance with IEC 62443 and related frameworks, to safeguard critical industrial assets, maintain resilient operations, and mitigate cyber risks across OT environments.

competencies.name: OT Downstream Cybersecurity
competencies.description: The ability to secure and protect operational technology (OT) systems in downstream oil and gas operations, including refining, petrochemical processing, and distribution, ensuring safe, resilient, and compliant production and delivery of petroleum products.

competencies.name: OT Incident Response & Forensics
competencies.description: The ability to manages OT cyber incident response coordinating containment, recovery, and forensics while maintaining safety and compliance with UAE critical infrastructure regulations and industry standards across different OT environments.

competencies.name: OT/ICS Security Assurance and IEC 62443 Conformance
competencies.description: The ability to plan and execute OT assurance that sustains IEC 62443 conformance, prioritises safety, and proves control effectiveness across plants, pipelines, and terminals.

competencies.name: OT KPIs & Dashboarding
competencies.description: The ability to develop and maintain OT security KPIs and dashboards that visualize risk, control performance, and compliance to support data-driven decisions aligned with UAE energy regulations and corporate cybersecurity standards.

competencies.name: OT Network Design
competencies.description: The ability to design and enforce OT network architectures using zoning and segmentation to block unauthorized traffic, protect SIS, and reduce lateral movement, aligned with IEC 62443 and corporate cybersecurity directives.

competencies.name: OT Project Security Validation
competencies.description: The ability to ensure OT cybersecurity requirements are embedded and verified across EPCC project phases, aligning with corporate standards, UAE regulations, and international ICS/SCADA security frameworks.

competencies.name: OT Patch & Vulnerability Management
competencies.description: The ability to identify, prioritize, and remediate vulnerabilities in OT environments while maintaining safety, minimizing production downtime, and meeting UAE regulatory and industry-specific compliance requirements.

competencies.name: OT Regulatory Compliance
competencies.description: The ability to ensure OT security control alignment with ISA/IEC 62443 and UAE regulations by managing compliance programs, audits, and evidence across critical infrastructure environments.

competencies.name: OT Security Baselines & Configuration Management
competencies.description: The ability to define, implement, and verify hardened security baselines for Operational Technology (OT) systems to reduce cyber risk and attack surface across critical assets.

competencies.name: OT Threat Detection & Monitoring
competencies.description: The ability to detects, analyze, and alert on threats across industrial networks and control systems to protect critical OT assets, aligned with UAE regulations, corporate standards, and energy sector threat intelligence frameworks.

competencies.name: OT Upstream Cybersecurity
competencies.description: The ability to secure and protect operational technology (OT) systems involved in upstream oil and gas operations (exploration and production) ensuring resilient and safe extraction processes in remote and distributed environments.

competencies.name: OPSEC Workplace (Covert Command-and-Control Resilience)
competencies.description: The ability to design and maintain resilient command-and-control (C) infrastructures (leveraging staging servers, proxy chains, domain fronting, and layered encryption) while enforcing rigorous operational-security (OPSEC) procedures to prevent attribution, frustrate defensive telemetry, and sustain undetected access during Red-Team operations.

competencies.name: Privileged Access Management (PAM) Governance
competencies.description: The ability to govern, assure, and monitor privileged access across IT, cloud, and OT, enforcing policy, evidencing compliance, and detecting misuse through structured reviews, session oversight, metrics, and continuous control monitoring.

competencies.name: Patch Compliance and Audit Readiness
competencies.description: The ability to analyze, prioritize, and manage vulnerabilities that drive patching decisions, ensuring remediation efforts focus on the highest-risk exposures.

competencies.name: PKI & Certificate Management
competencies.description: The ability to architect, implement, and govern cryptographic ecosystems, spanning certificate lifecycle management, public key infrastructure (PKI), and cloud encryption services, to ensure data confidentiality, integrity, and authenticity across distributed environments.

competencies.name: Privacy & Data Security Metrics/KPIs
competencies.description: The ability to define, capture, and visualize key privacy and data security indicators (e.g., DPIA completion rates, DLP incident trends, etc.) aligned with UAE regulatory mandates.

competencies.name: Patch Lifecyle and Release Management
competencies.description: The ability to manage the complete lifecycle of software patches, from vendor release through internal validation, controlled deployment, and decommissioning , to ensure timely, secure, and compliant updates across enterprise systems.

competencies.name: Patch Management
competencies.description: The ability to identify, prioritize, deploy, verify, and track security patches and compensating mitigations across IT, OT, and cloud environments, aligned with vulnerability risk, business impact, and compliance requirements. This includes leveraging automation, analytics, and AI to optimize remediation timelines and ensure evidence-based verification.

competencies.name: Preventive Maintenance for OT Security Platforms
competencies.description: The ability to implement preventive maintenance for OT security platforms, aligning with vendor guidance, UAE regulations, and oil and gas uptime requirements to ensure resilient, up-to-date cyber controls.

competencies.name: Patch Management Platform Operation
competencies.description: The ability to effectively use, configure, and optimize enterprise patch management platforms to plan, deploy, monitor, and report on system updates across Windows and Linux environments.

competencies.name: Policy, Procedure & Standards Development
competencies.description: The ability to design, document, deploy, and continuously improve cybersecurity policies, procedures, and standards, establishing clear governance, data-handling protocols, and regulatory alignment, so that all business units operate under consistent, auditable, and risk-appropriate controls across the policy lifecycle.

competencies.name: Patch Reporting, Analytics and Continuous Improvement
competencies.description: The ability to collect, analyze, and communicate patch management metrics to drive transparency, compliance, and ongoing performance enhancement.

competencies.name: Process-Safety & HSE Cyber-Risk Alignment
competencies.description: The ability to integrate cybersecurity risk into process safety and HSE frameworks to protect OT, SIS, and emergency systems, ensuring alignment with corporate standards and UAE regulatory requirements.

competencies.name: Penetration Testing
competencies.description: The ability to simulate cyberattacks against computer systems, networks, applications, and physical infrastructure to identify security vulnerabilities and help strengthen security posture.

competencies.name: Purple Team Engagement
competencies.description: The ability to operate effectively in joint Red Team (offense) and Blue Team (defense) exercises—planning, executing, and analyzing purple-team engagements to tune detections, close visibility gaps, validate security controls, and drive continuous-improvement of the organization's cyber-defence posture across IT and OT environments.

competencies.name: Risk Assessment Methodology
competencies.description: The ability to plan, execute, and govern structured risk assessments to identify, analyze, and evaluate threats, vulnerabilities, and business impacts across IT, OT, and organizational domains, aligning with global standards such as ISO 31000, ISO 27005, and ISO 22301 to inform decision-making and strengthen operational resilience.

competencies.name: Regulatory Compliance (IAM)
competencies.description: The ability to interpret regulatory requirements, industry standards, and audit obligations, translating them into effective IAM controls, evidence collection mechanisms, and attestation processes that demonstrably reduce risk and ensure continuous, verifiable compliance across the enterprise.

competencies.name: Regulatory Compliance & Standards Adherence
competencies.description: The ability to interpret, implement, monitor, and continuously improve cybersecurity requirements from international and national standards, sector directives, and contractual or legal obligations, ensuring that both OT and IT environments remain demonstrably compliant and resilient.

competencies.name: Red Team Management
competencies.description: The ability to plan, execute, govern, and evaluate Red Team operations, simulations, and adversary emulation activities to assess and improve the organization's cyber resilience, detection capabilities, and response effectiveness across IT and OT environments, in alignment with industry standards (e.g., MITRE ATT&CK, TIBER, NIST SP 800-115).

competencies.name: Risk Treatment & Mitigation Planning
competencies.description: The ability to develop, implement, and oversee risk treatment plans by selecting and applying controls, accepting or transferring risks as appropriate, and tracking remediation actions to mitigate identified cybersecurity risks and strengthen secure operations.

competencies.name: Red Team & Vulnerability Assessment Reporting
competencies.description: The ability to synthesise, document, and communicate findings from penetration tests, red-team exercises, and enterprise vulnerability assessments across converged OT and IT landscapes in the Oil & Gas sector articulating technical details, business risk, safety impact, and remediation priorities in clear, actionable formats for engineers, SOC teams, plant managers, and executive stakeholders.

competencies.name: SOC Automation
competencies.description: The ability to identify, implement, and optimize automated tools, workflows, and processes to manage to security threats and incidents with increased speed, consistency, and scalability while reducing manual effort and human error in security operations.

competencies.name: Security Awareness & Communication
competencies.description: The ability to ensures employees have the necessary knowledge and skills regarding cybersecurity risks and threats as well as the policies and best practices that apply within an organization.

competencies.name: Security Alert Triage
competencies.description: The ability to assess, validate, and prioritize security alerts based on contextual risk, ensuring timely escalation of true threats while minimizing false positives and maintaining efficient incident response workflows.

competencies.name: Security Control Compliance Assurance
competencies.description: The ability to assure cybersecurity controls implemented across OT and IT systems are effective, ensuring compliance with internal policies, international standards, and sector regulations.

competencies.name: Strategic Change Cyber Assurance
competencies.description: The ability to provide cybersecurity advisory and assurance across M&A, transformation, and digitization initiatives covering due diligence, control reviews, change-gating, and post-implementation testing to protect value, meet regulations, and align with risk appetite.

competencies.name: Server Configuration and Hardening
competencies.description: The ability to establish, implement, and maintain secure configuration baselines across Windows and Linux server environments to reduce attack surfaces and ensure system integrity.

competencies.name: Server Cyber Hygiene Monitoring and Reporting
competencies.description: The ability to ensure servers (Windows, Linux, on-prem, and cloud) are continuously monitored, assessed, and maintained for security health, configuration compliance, and vulnerability posture, with accurate, auditable reporting to stakeholders.

competencies.name: Strategic Cyber Risk Advisory
competencies.description: The ability to interpret, contextualize, and communicate cyber threat intelligence into actionable risk insights that inform executive decision-making, influence strategic investments, and align threat mitigation with organizational priorities.

competencies.name: Scenario Development & Resilience Simulation
competencies.description: The ability to design, script, and execute realistic disruption scenarios that test organizational readiness, surface hidden dependencies, and drive continuous improvement of business-continuity and disaster-recovery capabilities.

competencies.name: Social Engineering & Insider Threat Simulation
competencies.description: The ability to design and conduct sophisticated social-engineering and insider-threat campaigns to rigorously test human, process, and facility defences across IT and OT environments.

competencies.name: System Hardening and OS Cyber Hygiene
competencies.description: The ability to reduce attack surface by securely configuring operating systems, services and endpoints according to approved cybersecurity benchmarks.

competencies.name: Server Patch Deployment
competencies.description: The ability to plan, execute, and govern the timely deployment of operating system and third-party software updates across Windows and Linux server environments to ensure systems remain secure, stable, and compliant.

competencies.name: Secure Remote Access Gateway Administration
competencies.description: The ability to administer secure remote access gateways to OT assets, enabling controlled, auditable connectivity that preserves safety, system integrity, and compliance with UAE cybersecurity and sector-specific regulations.

competencies.name: Security Standards and Compliance Governance
competencies.description: The ability to interpret, implement, monitor, and continuously improve cybersecurity requirements from international standards, regional regulations, sector-specific directives, and contractual obligations, ensuring integrated cybersecurity controls across both IT and OT environments remain compliant.

competencies.name: Threat Actor Profiling
competencies.description: The ability to investigate, profile, and track threat actors targeting OT and IT technology in the Oil & Gas sector, transforming disparate data on campaigns, capabilities, and motivations into comprehensive actor profiles that inform risk assessments, detection logic, and strategic defence decisions.

competencies.name: Threat Emulation Planning & Execution
competencies.description: The ability to design, orchestrate, and conduct full-scope red-team operations that faithfully replicate advanced adversaries to achieve clearly defined intelligence or resilience-testing objectives.

competencies.name: Technology Evaluation & Resilience Architecture
competencies.description: The ability to assess, select, and architect technology solutions that support digital business continuity and cyber resilience objectives.

competencies.name: Threat Hunting
competencies.description: The ability to conduct hypothesis-driven searches for malicious activities and potential security compromises that may have evaded security controls within an organization's network and systems.

competencies.name: Threat Intelligence Deception Tooling
competencies.description: The ability to design, deploy, and maintain deception technologies inside IT and OT environments to lure, detect, and analyse adversary activity and disrupt campaigns before critical production systems are compromised.

competencies.name: Threat Intelligence Governance and Compliance
competencies.description: The ability to apply regulatory, ethical, and policy-based requirements to ensure threat intelligence activities are conducted responsibly, securely, and in alignment with organizational standards and industry frameworks.

competencies.name: Threat Intelligence Lifecycle Management
competencies.description: The ability to orchestrate end-to-end cyber-threat intelligence, from multi-source collection and enrichment through to enterprise-wide operationalisation, ensuring lifecycle quality assurance and the delivery of timely, actionable defence for OT/IT operations.

competencies.name: Threat Intelligence Program Development & Leadership
competencies.description: The ability to lead, develop, and sustain a high-performing threat intelligence function by setting vision and strategy, building capability, managing performance, and fostering continuous improvement aligned with organizational goals.

competencies.name: Threat Intelligence Reporting & Communication
competencies.description: The ability to create and deliver clear, contextualized, and actionable threat intelligence outputs tailored to diverse audiences, from technical teams to executive leadership (tactical, operational and strategic).

competencies.name: Threat Modelling
competencies.description: The ability to identify, model, and prioritise cyber-threat scenarios that could impact both OT and IT environments in Oil & Gas, translating adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) into structured threat models that guide detection engineering, risk mitigation, and business-continuity planning.

competencies.name: Threat Monitoring and Detection
competencies.description: The ability to monitor networks, systems, and data to detect potential security threats, vulnerabilities, and suspicious activities to help maintain a robust security posture and ensure a rapid response to security incidents.

competencies.name: Third-Party & Cross-Border Data Transfer Compliance
competencies.description: The ability to assess third-party data transfers, draft contract protections, and apply legal tools like SCCs and TIAs to manage cross-border data flows in line with UAE privacy laws and the organization's risk tolerance.

competencies.name: Tools and Scripting Creation
competencies.description: The ability to design, code, and maintain custom security tools, scripts, and automations that streamline defensive (SOC), offensive (Red-Team), and engineering workflows across converged IT/OT environments in the Oil & Gas sector, enabling rapid data collection, threat detection, exploitation testing, and incident response while upholding safety, reliability, and regulatory constraints.

competencies.name: Testing, Validation and Rollback Management
competencies.description: The ability to plan and govern patch testing and rollback procedures that ensure stability, minimize disruption, and maintain reliability through structured validation, regression checks, and safe recovery mechanisms.

competencies.name: User Provisioning
competencies.description: The ability to orchestrate, automate, and continuously improve joiner–mover–leaver (JML) workflows to ensure accurate, timely, and auditable creation, modification, and removal of user accounts, attributes, roles, and licenses across all systems.

competencies.name: Vulnerability Management
competencies.description: The ability to systematically detect, analyze, prioritize, and remediate vulnerabilities across IT, OT, and cloud environments using risk-based, automated, and threat-informed approaches. This includes integrating AI capabilities to improve detection accuracy, remediation speed, and prioritization efficiency.

competencies.name: Web and API Security
competencies.description: The ability to protect web applications and APIs against exploits, abuse and data leakage by applying secure-coding and defensive controls.

competencies.name: Wireless / Low-Bandwidth OT Field Asset Security
competencies.description: The ability to secure telemetry and control traffic over constrained or wireless links, ensuring data confidentiality, integrity, and availability across remote, low-bandwidth OT environments.

competencies.name: Windows and Linux Server Administration
competencies.description: The ability to effectively configure, maintain, secure, and troubleshoot Windows and Linux server environments that underpin enterprise operations and patch management activities.

competencies.name: Document Management
competencies.description: The ability to create, manage, and govern cybersecurity documentation (e.g. policies, standards, runbooks, threat-intel reports, code artifacts) using disciplined version-control and knowledge management practices that ensure accuracy, traceability, and continuous improvement across IT & OT environments.
